result.rationale: Verified in refreshOAuthTokens.ts: the outbound fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT posts only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in a URLSearchParams body with no Authorization header or CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, despite the inbound webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) requiring a secret header. The parent application receiving tokens has no cryptographic authentication shown in the diff, so the security of credential syncing relies on network isolation. This is a genuine security weakness introduced by the new code.

judged_text: No authentication on the outbound sync request: the request carries only calcomUserId + appSlug in the body — the shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not sent, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can request a user's access tokens; security relies entirely on network isolation of the parent app (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com POSTs to the external sync endpoint with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no auth headers/secret (no `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, no signature). The diff also introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/header-name but those are only used for the inbound webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not for this outbound sync call, so the parent app has no shared-secret-based way to authenticate the caller beyond network controls. This is a verifiable security defect exposed by the change.
